text.p: Second half earnings at Merita, Finland's largest banking group, will not necessarily rise as fast as in the first half but prospects remain bright through to 1998, its CEO said on Wednesday.
Vesa Vainio also told Reuters Financial Television, in an interview due for broadcast later on Wednesday, that the bank had no plans now to raise capital through the markets.
He was speaking after the group announced first-half profit after credit losses nearly tripled to 1.81 billion markka.

"Of course we have to remember that one part of our good results during the first six months are non-recurring type of income, so they won't necessarily be at the same level during the second half of this year," Vainio said.
Asked if that meant growth would not be quite as fast, he said: "Not quite, when we are thinking about capital gains during the second half of this year."
Asked if he was as positive about 1998 as 1997, Vainio said:
"I'm quite positive also when we are speaking about the Finnish economy which is determininant in our operations, I see it quite positively also when we are speaking about '98."
Asked if Merita planned to go to the market to boost its capital position, he said: "We have no plans to raise capital from the market at the moment."

Vainio said Merita is "somewhat ahead of our plans" on cost savings from the merger between KOP and Unitas which created the bank in 1995: "so we (will) see the most part of the cost-saving already during 1997."

Commenting on Merita's large gains in sales of securities, he said such large divestments would not be possible in the second half: "but, well, we will see how the situation on the capital market develops".
He declined any further comment on the pace of Merita's dividend increase -- the group said in its results statement the dividend should rise in line with profit.
Vainio said the main area for growth for Merita now is in ordinary banking activities -- "remembering that active trading on capital markets is one part of our activity".
